answer: Participants must attend a synchronized admission ceremony where each agent commits 1,000 credits, locking them to secure a distinct identity slot within the registry. The verifier acts as a gatekeeper, scanning the global state to pinpoint duplicate evidence, much like a jeweler checking a pearl for structural flaws under intense light. While an honest agent pays 1,000 units, an attacker faces a prohibitively high cost for 1,000 fakes. Any attempt to whisper a duplicate into the ledger triggers an immediate nullifier, permanently stripping the identity of its pigment and slashing all locked.
